added_models.model: Heterozygous carriers of SOST loss-of-function (sclerosteosis gene carriers)

efficacy.population: Unselected (postmenopausal women with low BMD or osteoporosis)
efficacy.note: Sclerosteosis carriers with one null SOST allele had higher BMD at every site without skeletal complications: a titrated-sclerostin model.
efficacy.quote: Heterozygous carriers of sclerosteosis have BMD values consistently higher than the mean of healthy subjects without any of the bone complications encountered in homozygotes.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry; the authors frame partial sclerostin loss as a model for osteoporosis therapeutics.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: BMD above age mean in carriers vs lumbar spine BMD gain on romosozumab
efficacy.population: Unselected (postmenopausal women with low BMD or osteoporosis)
efficacy.note: Partial sclerostin loss predicted higher BMD; romosozumab raised lumbar spine BMD 11.3% at 12 months in phase 2.
efficacy.short: Spine BMD rose, as carriers predicted
efficacy.quote: All dose levels of romosozumab were associated with significant increases in bone mineral density at the lumbar spine, including an increase of 11.3% with the 210-mg monthly dose, as compared with a decrease of 0.1% with placebo
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me with Gardner 2005. Carrier BMD Z-scores and a 12-month percent gain are not on one scale, so direction only; FRAME later positive on fracture.

safety.population: Unselected (postmenopausal women with low BMD or osteoporosis)
safety.note: Carriers showed none of the homozygotes' hyperostosis or nerve-compression complications, predicting partial inhibition spares them.
safety.quote: Heterozygous carriers of sclerosteosis have BMD values consistently higher than the mean of healthy subjects without any of the bone complications encountered in homozygotes.
safety.judgement: Opening entry; the stated prediction is the absence of hyperostotic complications.

safety.population: Unselected (postmenopausal women with low BMD or osteoporosis)
safety.confidence_note: FDA review text from the source bundle; quote is the first part of a longer sentence.
safety.note: FDA set the carrier phenotype against trial data: hyperostosis 0.5% on romosozumab vs 0.8% placebo, no excess neurological compression or hearing loss.
safety.short: No hyperostosis excess, as carriers predicted
safety.quote: In the 12-month placebo-controlled population, adverse events of hyperostosis were reported for 0.5% of subjects in the romosozumab treatment group and 0.8% of subjects in the placebo group
safety.judgement: The review states hyperostosis is a feature of homozygotes, not heterozygotes, beside the trial rates, so comparison_stated true. The same review notes no CV risk reported in sclerosteosis but calls the population too small to detect a modest increase; that silence is not scored as contra.

added_models.model: UK Biobank carriers of the SOST-lowering common allele rs2741856 (Amgen Study 150655)

efficacy.population: Unselected (postmenopausal women with low BMD or osteoporosis)
efficacy.confidence_note: FDA review text; study start date not public, 2019 review used as proxy for first use.
efficacy.note: Sponsor GWAS lookup run for the BLA resubmission after the ARCH CV imbalance; one SOST eQTL allele as a proxy for romosozumab.
efficacy.quote: In the database examined, no statistically significant genetic association was identified between risk of osteoporosis and fracture and risk of MI or stroke.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at the review's public date (proxy). Opening marker only; the comparison that follows is the retrodiction.

efficacy.population: Unselected (postmenopausal women with low BMD or osteoporosis)
efficacy.confidence_note: FDA review text; partial sentence quoted.
efficacy.note: The SOST-lowering allele carried lower osteoporosis and fracture risk, reproducing the known fracture benefit of romosozumab.
efficacy.short: Allele lowers fracture risk, as trials showed
efficacy.quote: genetically reduced SOST expression in aorta and tibial artery by a common SNP in the European population has a significant effect on BMD, osteoporosis and bone fracture

safety.population: Unselected (postmenopausal women with low BMD or osteoporosis)
safety.confidence_note: FDA review text; study start date not public, 2019 used as proxy.
safety.note: Sponsor GWAS lookup of MI and stroke in carriers of a SOST-lowering allele, run in response to the ARCH CV imbalance.
safety.quote: In the database examined, no statistically significant genetic association was identified between risk of osteoporosis and fracture and risk of MI or stroke.
safety.judgement: Opening entry at the review's public date (proxy). Opening marker only; the comparison that follows is the retrodiction.

safety.magnitude_basis: MI/stroke association (null, p>0.10) vs ARCH serious CV event imbalance
safety.population: Unselected (postmenopausal women with low BMD or osteoporosis)
safety.confidence_note: FDA review text; single SNP, eQTL in arterial tissue, no MR scaling; human CV signal itself inconsistent across FRAME and ARCH.
safety.note: The allele showed no MI or stroke effect, failing to reproduce the ARCH cardiovascular imbalance that became a boxed warning.
safety.short: No CV signal; trials showed one
safety.quote: In the database examined, no statistically significant genetic association was identified between risk of osteoporosis and fracture and risk of MI or stroke.
safety.reason: Missed the CV signal in patients
safety.judgement: Judgement call: a retrodiction that failed to reproduce the labeled CV harm is contra. FDA kept the boxed warning, reading the genetic data as not clearly indicating an association, not as exoneration.

added_models.model: Mendelian randomization with SOST-locus variants scaled to romosozumab 210 mg

efficacy.population: Unselected (postmenopausal women with low BMD or osteoporosis)
efficacy.note: SOST BMD-raising variants scaled to romosozumab's BMD effect, used to mimic therapeutic sclerostin inhibition.
efficacy.quote: the SOST genetic variants were associated with lower risk of fracture and osteoporosis (commensurate with the therapeutic effect of romosozumab) and with a higher risk of myocardial infarction and/or coronary revascularization and major adverse cardiovascular events.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry; the model was built after the trials reported. Opening marker only; the comparison that follows is the retrodiction.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: genetic fracture risk reduction scaled to 210 mg vs trial effect, as the authors state commensurate
efficacy.population: Unselected (postmenopausal women with low BMD or osteoporosis)
efficacy.note: Variants scaled to 210 mg monthly carried lower fracture and osteoporosis risk, commensurate with romosozumab's trial effect.
efficacy.quote: the SOST genetic variants were associated with lower risk of fracture and osteoporosis (commensurate with the therapeutic effect of romosozumab) and with a higher risk of myocardial infarction and/or coronary revascularization and major adverse cardiovascular events.
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction, run after FRAME/ARCH; the paper itself places genetic and trial effects side by side. Alcalde-Herraiz 2024 (doi 10.1038/s41467-024-53623-5, pQTL instruments) reproduced the bone benefit again; no status change.

safety.population: Unselected (postmenopausal women with low BMD or osteoporosis)
safety.note: The same scaled SOST variants tested against MI, coronary revascularization and MACE.
safety.quote: the SOST genetic variants were associated with lower risk of fracture and osteoporosis (commensurate with the therapeutic effect of romosozumab) and with a higher risk of myocardial infarction and/or coronary revascularization and major adverse cardiovascular events.
safety.judgement: Opening entry; built after the ARCH imbalance. Opening marker only; the comparison that follows is the retrodiction.

safety.magnitude_basis: genetic MI/MACE risk vs meta-analysed trial CV events
safety.population: Unselected (postmenopausal women with low BMD or osteoporosis)
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC). Thorolfsdottir 2026 (doi 10.1093/hmg/ddaf177) found no CV association with plasma-sclerostin pQTL instruments that also failed the bone positive control; not scored.
safety.note: Variants mimicking 210 mg raised MI/revascularization and MACE risk, reproducing the trials' probable CV excess.
safety.quote: the SOST genetic variants were associated with lower risk of fracture and osteoporosis (commensurate with the therapeutic effect of romosozumab) and with a higher risk of myocardial infarction and/or coronary revascularization and major adverse cardiovascular events.
safety.judgement: Retrodiction reproducing the human CV signal is retro. Alcalde-Herraiz 2024 (pQTL instruments) also found 25-85% excess CAD risk: no status change. Thorolfsdottir 2026 null CV result set aside because its instruments did not move bone, so they do not proxy inhibition.

efficacy.population: Unselected (postmenopausal women with low BMD or osteoporosis)
efficacy.note: Romosozumab itself given to estrogen-deficient monkeys for 12 months; published three months after FRAME.
efficacy.quote: Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) bone mineral density (BMD) was increased by 14% to 26% at the lumbar spine and proximal femur at month 12
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry; a distinct system from the draft's gonad-intact Scl-AbIV monkey (OVX, the product itself, 12 months). Opening marker only; the comparison that follows is the retrodiction.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: 12-month lumbar spine BMD gain, monkey 14-26% vs human 11.3% (210 mg)
efficacy.population: Unselected (postmenopausal women with low BMD or osteoporosis)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level. Model epub Dec 2016, after phase 2 (2014) and FRAME (Sept 2016).
efficacy.note: Spine and femur BMD rose 14-26% at 12 months, reproducing the 11.3% spine gain already reported in phase 2.
efficacy.quote: All dose levels of romosozumab were associated with significant increases in bone mineral density at the lumbar spine, including an increase of 11.3% with the 210-mg monthly dose, as compared with a decrease of 0.1% with placebo
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me; a retrodiction because the human BMD and fracture results were public before the monkey paper. Year set to the model's epub, when the pairing became possible.

added_models.model: Angiotensin II-infused ApoE-knockout mouse with SOST transgene or recombinant sclerostin

safety.population: Unselected (postmenopausal women with low BMD or osteoporosis)
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC); epub 2016-12-22, before the ARCH CV imbalance was public (May 2017).
safety.note: Raising sclerostin suppressed aortic aneurysm and atherosclerosis in AngII ApoE-/- mice, implying sclerostin inhibition could worsen vascular disease.
safety.quote: Transgenic introduction of human SOST in apolipoprotein E-deficient (ApoE-/-) mice (SOSTTg .ApoE-/-) and administration of recombinant mouse Sost inhibited angiotensin II-induced AA and atherosclerosis.
safety.judgement: Opening entry; the model raised sclerostin rather than blocking it, so the harm prediction for inhibitors is an inference, which FDA drew in its review.

safety.magnitude_basis: aneurysm/atherosclerosis protection by sclerostin vs serious CV events on romosozumab
safety.population: Unselected (postmenopausal women with low BMD or osteoporosis)
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level. The mouse readout (aneurysm, plaque) is not the human event (MI, stroke); FRAME vs placebo showed no imbalance.
safety.note: ARCH then showed more adjudicated serious CV events on romosozumab than alendronate, in the direction the mouse implied.
safety.short: CV excess in ARCH, as mouse implied
safety.quote: During year 1, positively adjudicated serious cardiovascular adverse events were observed more often with romosozumab than with alendronate (50 of 2040 patients [2.5%] vs. 38 of 2014 patients [1.9%]).
safety.judgement: Judgement call: paired by me; the FDA review cites Krishna beside the clinical CV concern without stating a match. Prospective by five months, so same rather than retro, partial because aneurysm was not the human harm.

considered_not_added: Thorolfsdottir 2026 plasma-sclerostin pQTL MR (doi 10.1093/hmg/ddaf177): instruments failed the bone positive control, so not a proxy for inhibition; noted on the MR track, not scored
Zheng 2023 Arthritis Rheumatol sclerostin GWAS/MR (lower sclerostin and atherosclerosis risk): not looked up within budget; same system as the MR track and would not change its retro status
Blosozumab injection-site reactions and phase 3 stop: no model predicted local tolerance in a public source; patient-side only
Setrusumab: its admissible model-patient comparisons are in osteogenesis imperfecta (Brtl/+ and Crtap-/- mice), another disease, so outside this context
SOST knockout mouse (Li 2008): target-validation genetic model; not searched within budget and would duplicate the rat/monkey efficacy tracks in direction
Romosozumab exposure-response / popPK models for dose selection: none with a stated pre-trial human target found in the FDA review grep or searches; not verified further
Patient-derived cells, PDX, ex-vivo sensitivity and challenge models: not applicable to an anabolic osteoporosis antibody; none found
Sclerosteosis/van Buchem patients and CV risk (FDA review, Beighton communications): too few subjects to show a modest CV increase; mentioned on the carrier track, not scored
